claim: For local coordination tasks, topologies that preserve neighborhood structure achieve higher success; for strict global agreement, fully connected topology is the only structure that succeeds consistently, while no single topology achieves robust performance across all coordination tasks.
falsifier: Test different coordination topologies on local and global agreement tasks; the claim predicts that neighborhood-preserving topologies will perform best on local tasks, fully connected will perform best on global agreement, and no topology will be best across all tasks.

exclusions: limited to the reported coordination tasks and topologies; transfer beyond them is unestablished

title: Coordination topology–coordination success boundary
